config.title: Component Composition

intro.title: Component Composition
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile card by combining smaller, reusable React components. You will learn component composition, a core React pattern where you assemble complex UIs from simpler building blocks. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and JSX for structuring the UI. By the end, you'll understand how to pass data between components and structure your app for better reusability and maintainability.
intro.usecase: Component composition is the foundational pattern for building complex, maintainable UIs in modern web applications. You see it in action in product dashboards, where modular panels for charts, tables, and metrics are assembled into a cohesive layout. It's essential for creating reusable, customizable UI elements like navigation menus, data filters, or modal dialogs, allowing developers to efficiently construct and manage large-scale interfaces like admin panels or e-commerce product pages.

objectives: Construct a parent component that renders multiple child components.
Configure child components by passing props from a parent component.
Manipulate component structure by nesting components within JSX.
Initialize and pass data objects as props to composed components.
Integrate reusable UI components to build a complex interface.
Render dynamic content by mapping arrays to component instances.
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define and enforce prop types in composition.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for a React TypeScript component with state are added.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not correct. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed with the lesson.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns null for now. Use TypeScript typing.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Remember to export it.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional App component is defined with proper TypeScript typing and exported.
successCriteria: The App component is created as a function that returns null and is exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named App, returns null, and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check the name, return value, and export.

steps.title: Define the Card component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Card that accepts title and content as props. The component should return a div element with the title in an h2 and content in a p.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named Card that takes props as an argument. Use destructuring to get title and content from props, then return JSX with these values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Card component is defined with typed props and returns JSX displaying title and content.
successCriteria: Card component is defined with title and content props, uses destructuring, and returns a div containing h2 and p elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your Card component accepts both title and content props and returns the correct JSX structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a component named Card with proper props and JSX return.

steps.title: Define the Header component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Header that accepts a title prop of type string and returns an <h1> element containing that title.
steps.hint: Define a component with props using TypeScript interface or inline type annotation. Return JSX with the title prop inside an <h1>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Header component is defined with proper TypeScript prop typing that renders the title in an <h1> element.
successCriteria:
Header component is created with a title prop of type string and returns

{title}

.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but check: does it accept a title prop with type string? Does it return an <h1> element containing the title?
steps.feedbackWrong: The Header component isn't defined correctly. Make sure to create a functional component named Header that accepts a title prop and returns an <h1> element.

steps.title: Initialize visibility state in App
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, initialize boolean state with useState. Name the state variable isVisible and the setter setIsVisible, with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Use const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState<boolean>(false) inside App.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing boolean state
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component has isVisible state initialized to false.
successCriteria: A boolean useState hook is created inside App with isVisible and setIsVisible, initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Close. Add boolean visibility state with isVisible and setIsVisible initialized to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState<boolean>(false) inside the App component.

steps.title: Define a handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a function named handleToggle that toggles the isVisible state value when called.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setter from useState to update the state. Remember to use the correct TypeScript type for the function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now contains a properly typed handler function that toggles the isVisible state.
successCriteria: A function named handleToggle is defined inside the App component and correctly toggles the isVisible state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named handleToggle and properly toggles the isVisible state using setIsVisible.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler function is missing or doesn't toggle the state correctly. Check the function name and implementation.

steps.title: Add Header and first Card to App
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, render Header first, followed by one Card component with title and content props.
steps.hint: Use a React fragment or wrapper, then place <Header title="Component Composition Demo" /> followed by one <Card title=... content=... />.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component renders Header and one Card as the initial composed UI.
successCriteria: The App return contains Header and one Card component with title and content props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the Header component is properly included in the return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Header component isn't yet included in the App component's return statement. Try adding <Header /> inside the return.

steps.title: Add a second Card component with different props
steps.instruction: In the App component's return statement, add another Card component after the first one with different title and content prop values.
steps.hint: Add a second <Card /> JSX element with different string values for the title and content props.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: using the same component with different props
<Card title="Second Card" content="This is different content" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will render two Card components with different content.
successCriteria: A second Card component is added with different title and content prop values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a second Card component, but make sure both title and content props have different values than the first Card.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a second Card component with different title and content prop values.

steps.title: Add a button and wire it to the handler
steps.instruction: In your App component's return statement, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls your toggle handler function, and add a paragraph that conditionally renders content based on the isVisible state.

steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a button that toggles the visibility state and a paragraph that appears when isVisible is true.
successCriteria: A button element with onClick={handleToggle} is added, and a conditional paragraph using isVisible state is present in the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the button with onClick handler and the conditional paragraph that uses isVisible.
